intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. Engage with fishmongers and food artisans who have operated here for generations, offering an authentic taste of Tokyo's legendary seafood and culinary culture.

experiences.name: Odaiba Waterfront Tech & Culture Experience
experiences.description: Visit the futuristic Odaiba island on Tokyo Bay, exploring teamLab Borderless digital art museum, the Toyota Mega Web showroom, and the Miraikan National Museum of Emerging Science. The beachfront setting of Odaiba Beach adds a coastal atmosphere unique to Tokyo, blending cutting-edge tech culture with waterfront leisure.

experiences.name: Akihabara Electric Town Deep Dive
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Tokyo's legendary electronics and pop culture district. Browse multi-floor electronics stores, retro game shops, anime merchandise outlets, and maid cafes. This neighborhood is the global epicenter of tech consumer culture and otaku subculture, offering a sensory overload of innovation and fandom.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Begin at Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, walking through the Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and snacks. Explore the surrounding Asakusa district for rickshaw rides, kimono rentals, and visits to local izakayas for yakitori and sake, deeply connecting with Edo-period Japanese heritage.

experiences.name: Shibuya & Harajuku Street Food & Culture Crawl
experiences.description: Navigate the vibrant streets of Shibuya and Harajuku, crossing the world-famous Shibuya Scramble and exploring Takeshita Street's quirky fashion scene. Indulge in crepes, ramen, and conveyor-belt sushi at local eateries, then visit Meiji Shrine for a serene cultural contrast. This experience encapsulates modern Tokyo's dynamic blend of youth culture, tradition, and gastronomy.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo, Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — skip morning slot. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the budget-friendly Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Tsukiji area. Check in to the boutique stay in Tsukiji, Chuo City and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short walk to the famous Tsukiji Outer Market (仲見世通り周辺) — browse fresh seafood stalls, tamagoyaki (egg) shops, and kitchen tool vendors. Get oriented with the neighborhood and pick up a light snack. Stroll along the Sumida River waterfront for a relaxing first look at Tokyo.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Tsukiji's local dining alleys for dinner. Walk to nearby Ginza (15 min on foot) to window-shop the upscale district at night — free and dazzling. Return to hotel early to rest after the long flight.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a convenience store onigiri (rice ball) at 7-Eleven or FamilyMart near the hotel (¥150–200)
meals.lunch: Grab a tamagoyaki skewer or fresh tuna handroll at Tsukiji Outer Market stalls (¥300–600)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market area ramen or donburi shop — try a local teishoku (set meal) for around ¥800–1,200

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light due to arrival at 13:00 and potential jet lag. Buy a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless train and bus travel throughout the trip. 1 USD ≈ 150 JPY; budget ¥3,000–4,000 for today.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tsukiji Outer Market early (opens ~5:00 AM, best by 8–9 AM) for the full fresh seafood breakfast experience. Try uni (sea urchin), ikura (salmon roe), or a classic tuna sashimi breakfast bowl at one of the market's small counter restaurants.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway (Hibiya Line, ~10 min) to Akihabara — Tokyo's legendary Electric Town. Explore multi-floor electronics shops (Yodobashi Camera, Sofmap), retro game stores, manga shops, and anime figure stores. Visit a maid café for a quirky cultural experience (budget entry ~¥500 + drink).
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner in the side streets. Explore the neon-lit arcades (game centers) in the evening — many games cost only ¥100 per play.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market seafood breakfast bowl (kaisendon) at a market stall counter — ¥1,000–1,500
meals.lunch: Akihabara side-street curry rice or katsu curry set meal — ¥700–1,000
meals.dinner: Ramen shop near Akihabara station — try Ichiran or a local independent shop for ¥800–1,200

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is the heart of Tokyo's tech and otaku culture — perfect for tech culture interest. Many shops open by 10–11 AM. Free to browse all stores. Bring cash as some small shops don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Asakusa (Taito City) via subway (~15 min from Tsukiji). Visit Senso-ji Temple (浅草寺) — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple. Walk through Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional snacks and souvenirs. Arrive early (before 9 AM) to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the backstreets of Asakusa for traditional craft shops (Kappabashi Kitchenware Street is a short walk away — the world's largest concentration of cooking supply shops, free to browse). Visit the Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center rooftop (free) for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Take the Tobu Skytree Line one stop to Tokyo Skytree area. Admire the tower from outside (entry is pricey — skip the observation deck to save budget). Stroll along the Sumida River with illuminated Skytree views. Return to Tsukiji via Asakusa.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near hotel — onigiri + coffee ¥300–400
meals.lunch: Asakusa soba or tempura set at a local restaurant near Senso-ji — ¥900–1,200
meals.dinner: Asakusa izakaya (Japanese pub) — order small plates (yakitori skewers, edamame, tofu) with draft beer. Budget ¥1,500–2,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter and stunning, especially in morning light. April may bring late cherry blossoms — Sumida Park nearby is a top hanami (blossom viewing) spot. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take the JR Yamanote Line to Harajuku station. Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine (明治神宮) — a serene forested Shinto shrine in the middle of the city. Free entry, peaceful walk through towering torii gates and cedar forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Meiji Jingu to Takeshita Street (竹下通り) — Harajuku's famous youth fashion street. Browse quirky fashion boutiques, crepe stands, and candy shops. Then walk through Omotesando (Tokyo's Champs-Élysées) for free architecture and window shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya (10-min walk from Omotesando). Watch the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing — one of the world's busiest pedestrian crossings. Visit the free observation deck at Shibuya Sky or view from the free Mag's Park terrace at Shibuya 109 area.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku crepe from a Takeshita Street stall — ¥500–700 (eat as a late breakfast/snack)
meals.lunch: Harajuku or Omotesando side-street lunch — try a budget bento box or gyudon (beef bowl) at Yoshinoya/Matsuya for ¥500–700
meals.dinner: Shibuya izakaya or conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) — budget ¥1,000–1,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free. Takeshita Street is best on weekends for full atmosphere. Shibuya Scramble is most dramatic at night. Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Yanaka (谷中) neighborhood — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) districts. Explore Yanaka Ginza shopping street, old temples, and traditional wooden houses. Visit Yanaka Cemetery (free, beautiful and historic).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Nezu Shrine (根津神社) — a stunning Edo-period shrine with hundreds of torii gates (similar to Fushimi Inari but much less crowded). Free entry. Then explore Nezu and Sendagi neighborhoods for vintage shops and local cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tsukiji area. Explore the local Tsukiji neighborhood at night — try a standing sushi bar (tachinomi style) or a small local izakaya for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza street food — try menchi katsu (fried meat croquette) from a local butcher stall ¥200–300
meals.lunch: Yanaka area small restaurant — handmade soba or udon set ¥800–1,000
meals.dinner: Tsukiji local standing sushi bar — fresh nigiri pieces from ¥100–200 each; budget ¥1,200–1,800

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is a wonderful off-the-beaten-path cultural experience — great for culture interest. Sunday morning is lively at Yanaka Ginza. Nezu Shrine's tunnel of torii gates is photogenic and completely free.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ueno Park (上野公園) — Tokyo's largest public park. Walk through the park, see Shinobazu Pond, and visit the free Tosho-gu Shrine. Browse the park's street vendors. Consider visiting the Tokyo National Museum exterior (entry ¥1,000 if interested in Japanese history and art).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ameyoko Market (アメ横) — a bustling open-air market street under the JR tracks near Ueno station. Great for cheap snacks, fresh food, discount clothing, and cosmetics. Very lively and authentic Tokyo market experience.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Akihabara (short walk or one subway stop from Ueno) for evening electronics and anime shopping. Visit a multi-story arcade game center for entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel area café — ¥300–500
meals.lunch: Ameyoko Market street food — fresh seafood, yakitori, or takoyaki stalls ¥500–800
meals.dinner: Ueno area ramen — try a local tonkotsu or miso ramen shop ¥800–1,000

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum (¥1,000) is optional but highly recommended for culture interest — it houses the world's largest collection of Japanese art. Ameyoko is free to browse and great for budget snacking.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island. Take the Yurikamome automated driverless monorail from Shimbashi (scenic ride with great bay views, ¥330). Visit teamLab Borderless digital art museum (book in advance, ¥3,200) OR explore the free outdoor areas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Odaiba's free attractions: DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (see the giant 1:1 scale Gundam statue outside — free), Odaiba Seaside Park waterfront, and the view of Rainbow Bridge. Visit DECKS Tokyo Beach mall for free browsing and retro Joypolis arcade.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset and Rainbow Bridge illumination from Odaiba beach (free and spectacular). Take the scenic Yurikamome back to Shimbashi, then return to Tsukiji.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near Shimbashi station — ¥300–400
meals.lunch: Odaiba food court at DiverCity or Aqua City mall — ramen, curry, or Japanese set meal ¥900–1,200
meals.dinner: Return to Tsukiji area — fresh sushi or donburi at a local restaurant ¥1,000–1,500

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless is a must for tech culture interest but costs ¥3,200 — allocate budget accordingly. The Gundam statue outside DiverCity is completely free. Odaiba has stunning views of Tokyo Bay and the city skyline.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku — take the subway to Shinjuku station (one of the world's busiest). Explore Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500 entry) — one of Tokyo's most beautiful parks, especially gorgeous in late cherry blossom season.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku's famous neighborhoods: Kabukicho (Tokyo's entertainment district — safe to walk in daytime), Golden Gai (tiny atmospheric bar alley with ~200 micro-bars, fascinating to walk through), and Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane — tiny alley of yakitori stalls under the tracks).
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Shinjuku for dinner in Omoide Yokocho. Experience the atmospheric smoky yakitori alley at night. Visit the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation decks (open until 10:30 PM, completely free, stunning night views).

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji area convenience store or local bakery — ¥300–500
meals.lunch: Shinjuku budget lunch — try a basement depachika (department store food floor) bento or standing soba shop ¥600–900
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho yakitori — skewers from ¥150–300 each; budget ¥1,500–2,000 including drinks

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is FREE and rivals paid observation decks — one of the best budget views in Tokyo. Shinjuku Gyoen is worth the ¥500 entry fee. Golden Gai is best explored in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Koenji (高円寺) neighborhood — a bohemian, counter-culture district known for vintage clothing shops, independent music venues, and local cafés. Very different from tourist Tokyo — authentic local neighborhood feel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Browse Koenji's famous vintage and second-hand clothing shops (some of the best in Tokyo, very affordable). Walk to nearby Asagaya for a quieter local shopping street. Visit Zenpukuji Park for a relaxing nature break.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Nakameguro (中目黒) for the evening — walk along the Meguro River canal, lined with cherry trees and boutique shops. Very photogenic especially at night with lantern lights. Browse independent shops and cafés.

meals.breakfast: Koenji local café breakfast — toast set (モーニング) with coffee, egg, and toast ¥500–700
meals.lunch: Koenji neighborhood curry or ramen shop — ¥700–1,000
meals.dinner: Nakameguro riverside café or izakaya — ¥1,200–1,800

day_by_day.notes: Koenji is a fantastic off-the-beaten-path local culture experience. Great for finding unique vintage items at low prices. Nakameguro is trendy but has affordable dining options in side streets away from the main canal.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Akihabara again for a deeper dive — explore the upper floors of Yodobashi Camera (massive tech megastore), visit retro game shops (Super Potato is legendary), and browse the dense electronics component shops on the side streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Nature and Science in Ueno (科学博物館) — excellent museum covering Japanese science and technology history (¥630 entry, great value). Highly relevant for tech culture interest.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Kanda and Jimbocho neighborhood — Tokyo's famous used bookstore district with hundreds of second-hand book, manga, and art print shops. Great for browsing even without buying.

meals.breakfast: Akihabara area convenience store or fast food — ¥300–500
meals.lunch: Akihabara curry restaurant — Japanese-style curry rice set ¥700–900
meals.dinner: Jimbocho area — try a local Japanese restaurant or budget soba shop ¥800–1,200

day_by_day.notes: National Museum of Nature and Science is excellent value at ¥630. Super Potato retro game shop in Akihabara is a must for tech culture fans. Jimbocho bookstore district is free to browse and uniquely Tokyo.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tsukiji Fish Market area one more time for a proper morning market breakfast. Then head to nearby Hamarikyu Gardens (浜離宮恩賜庭園) — a beautiful traditional Japanese garden with a tidal pond, right next to the hotel. Entry ¥300.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the water bus (¥1,040) from Hamarikyu Gardens along the Sumida River to Asakusa — a scenic and unique way to travel. Explore Asakusa's craft and traditional goods shops again, or visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum (江戸東京博物館) nearby (¥600) for deep Japanese cultural history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tsukiji for a farewell dinner in the neighborhood. Explore the local streets and pick up any last souvenirs at the outer market area.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh seafood and tamagoyaki breakfast ¥800–1,200
meals.lunch: Asakusa tempura teishoku set meal at a local restaurant ¥1,000–1,400
meals.dinner: Tsukiji local izakaya — celebrate with a proper Japanese multi-course izakaya meal ¥2,000–2,500

day_by_day.notes: The water bus from Hamarikyu to Asakusa is a scenic and memorable experience — worth the ¥1,040 fare. Hamarikyu Gardens at ¥300 is great value. Edo-Tokyo Museum (if open — check for renovation schedule) is excellent for culture interest.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shimokitazawa (下北沢) — Tokyo's hippest bohemian neighborhood known for vintage shops, live music venues, indie theaters, and local cafés. Explore the narrow streets and browse second-hand clothing stores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Daikanyama T-Site (代官山 蔦屋書店) — a stunning architectural bookstore and cultural complex. Free to browse. Walk to nearby Ebisu and visit Yebisu Beer Museum (free entry, paid tasting ¥500 optional) — great for tech/industrial culture interest.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Tokyo — head back to Shinjuku or Shibuya for a memorable last night out. Revisit a favorite spot, pick up last-minute souvenirs at Don Quijote (discount variety store, open 24 hours), and enjoy the city lights.

meals.breakfast: Shimokitazawa local café morning set — ¥500–700
meals.lunch: Shimokitazawa vintage market food stalls or local curry shop — ¥700–1,000
meals.dinner: Shinjuku or Shibuya farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a nicer izakaya or Japanese BBQ (yakiniku) ¥2,000–3,000

day_by_day.notes: Shimokitazawa is best on weekends when flea markets and street events are active. Don Quijote (Donki) is the best place for affordable last-minute souvenirs, snacks, and gifts. Stay out as late as you like — Tokyo is safe 24/7.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo. Take a last walk through Tsukiji Outer Market for a farewell breakfast. Pick up any final food souvenirs — packaged Japanese snacks, tea, or condiments make great gifts and are very affordable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel (most check-outs by 11:00 AM — store luggage at the hotel or a coin locker at the nearest train station). Spend remaining time in the Ginza area (5-min walk) — browse the free Itoya stationery flagship store or the Ginza Six mall atrium. Head to the airport via Narita Express or bus.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo. Reflect on 13 incredible days of food, tech, and culture in one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market final seafood breakfast — ¥1,000–1,500
meals.lunch: Ginza area convenience store or underground mall bento — ¥500–700 (light before flight)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport travel and check-in. Narita Express (N'EX) takes ~60–90 min from Shinjuku/Tokyo station; Limousine Bus takes ~90–120 min. Redeem any leftover Suica card balance at airport kiosks or keep it for a future visit.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo, Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport at 13:00 — clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the airport limousine bus or express train to Tsukiji, Chuo City. Check in to your boutique hotel and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a relaxed stroll through the Tsukiji Outer Market (仲見世通り周辺) — still bustling with vendors selling tamagoyaki, fresh seafood snacks, pickles, and kitchenware. Get your bearings in the neighborhood and grab a light snack from a street stall.
day_by_day.evening: Walk 10 minutes to Hamarikyu Gardens for the late-afternoon golden hour view of the tidal pond and Tokyo skyline. Then head to nearby Ginza for a gentle evening walk along Chuo-dori, admiring the illuminated flagship stores.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick set meal at a soba shop inside Narita/Haneda airport or en route
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market area: try Sushi Zanmai (24-hour sushi chain, mid-range) for fresh nigiri — budget ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag is real — keep Day 1 light. Buy a Suica/Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip. April means cherry blossoms may still be visible in Hamarikyu Gardens.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Tsukiji Outer Market for a traditional Japanese breakfast — fresh tuna sashimi, grilled scallops, and tamago sushi straight from the vendors. Then walk to Hamarikyu Gardens (opens 9:00) for a peaceful morning stroll among spring blooms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Asakusa (20 min). Explore Senso-ji Temple, Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional souvenirs, and the surrounding Asakusa culture district. Visit the Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center rooftop for free panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Tokyo Skytree (15-min walk from Asakusa) for sunset and evening views from the observation deck (Tembo Deck at 350m). Explore the Solamachi shopping complex at the base.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market: fresh sashimi breakfast set at Daiwa Sushi or a vendor stall (~¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Asakusa: Kaminarimon area — try Asakusa Imahan for sukiyaki lunch set or Sometaro for okonomiyaki (~¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Skytree Solamachi: Rokurinsha ramen (famous Tokyo-style tsukemen) or a restaurant in the tower mall (~¥1,200–¥2,000)

day_by_day.notes: Book Tokyo Skytree tickets online in advance to avoid long queues. Tembo Deck tickets ~¥2,100 per adult.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Akihabara (Electric Town) — Tokyo's iconic tech and anime district. Spend the morning exploring multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Akiba and Sofmap, retro game shops, and the latest gadget stores. Immerse in cutting-edge consumer tech culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akihabara Radio Kaikan building for vintage electronics and collectibles. Then head to the nearby 3331 Arts Chiyoda, a creative tech-art space in a converted school. Walk to Kanda Myojin Shrine — surprisingly serene amid the electronics chaos — which is famous for tech blessings.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a maid café in Akihabara (budget ¥1,500–¥3,000 for drinks and a show) for a quintessential Tokyo pop culture experience. Then explore the evening neon-lit streets of Akihabara.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby Tsukiji café — try a Japanese morning set (coffee + toast + egg) at a local kissaten (~¥600–¥900)
meals.lunch: Akihabara: Curry House CoCo Ichibanya for Japanese curry or a basement food court set meal (~¥900–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Akihabara: Kanda area — try Kanda Yabu Soba (historic soba restaurant since 1880) for authentic hand-cut soba (~¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best on weekdays — weekends bring larger crowds. Some maid cafés require reservations; walk-ins usually available on Friday evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Ueno Park for a morning walk — in mid-April, late cherry blossoms or fresh green leaves create a beautiful atmosphere. Visit the Tokyo National Museum (opens 9:30), Japan's largest museum with an extraordinary collection of samurai armor, pottery, and Buddhist art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ueno's Ameyoko Market — a lively open-air market street with street food, fresh produce, clothing, and cosmetics. Then visit Yanaka Ginza, a preserved old-town shopping street with traditional crafts and local snacks — a rare glimpse of pre-war Tokyo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Ginza area near your hotel. Explore the Itoya stationery flagship store (9 floors of beautiful Japanese paper and design goods). Stroll Ginza's upscale streets and enjoy the Saturday evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Ueno area: convenience store (7-Eleven or Lawson) Japanese breakfast — onigiri, tamagoyaki, and green tea (~¥500)
meals.lunch: Ameyoko Market: street food crawl — yakitori, taiyaki, fresh fruit skewers (~¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Ginza: Ginza Kagari for refined chicken paitan ramen (small but excellent, ~¥1,200) or Kyubey sushi for a mid-range omakase (~¥5,000–¥8,000)

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum closed on Mondays. Yanaka Ginza is very photogenic — bring your camera. Ginza dining can be pricey; Kagari ramen offers great value in this upscale district.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Harajuku (40 min by subway). Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine early morning for a tranquil Shinto experience amid forested grounds. Witness the Sunday morning ceremony if timing aligns.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita-dori for Harajuku street fashion culture and quirky snacks (crepes, cotton candy burgers). Then head to Omotesando — Tokyo's 'Champs-Élysées' — for stylish architecture, boutique shopping, and the Omotesando Hills complex designed by Tadao Ando.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Shibuya (15 min). Experience the world-famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing at peak evening hours. Visit the Shibuya Sky observation deck for a 360° rooftop view of Tokyo at night (~¥2,000). Explore Shibuya's vibrant nightlife streets.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku: Bread, Espresso & for artisan coffee and croissants — a beloved local café (~¥800–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Omotesando: Gyukatsu Motomura for crispy beef cutlet set meal (~¥1,500–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Shibuya: Ichiran Ramen (solo dining ramen booths, a unique Tokyo experience) (~¥1,200) or Shibuya Hikarie food floors (~¥2,000–¥3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Book Shibuya Sky tickets online — they sell out quickly on weekends. Meiji Jingu is free to enter. Harajuku Takeshita-dori is most vibrant on Sunday afternoons.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island. Take the scenic Yurikamome driverless monorail from Shimbashi (15 min from Tsukiji). Visit teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets (book in advance) — immersive digital art experiences that perfectly blend tech and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Odaiba's DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (home to the life-size Gundam statue), Palette Town, and the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) featuring ASIMO robots and future technology exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset over Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo Bay from Odaiba beach promenade. Take the Yurikamome back and stop at Shimbashi for dinner in a classic salaryman izakaya district.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or Tsukiji area kissaten Japanese morning set (~¥700)
meals.lunch: Odaiba: Decks Tokyo Beach food court — try a ramen or Japanese curry set (~¥1,200–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Shimbashi: Standing izakaya (tachinomi) — yakitori skewers, edamame, and draft beer in a lively after-work atmosphere (~¥2,000–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets must be booked online well in advance (~¥3,200 per person). Miraikan is closed on Tuesdays. Odaiba is best visited on a clear day for bay views.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku — start with the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (free, opens 9:00) for panoramic city views including Mt. Fuji on clear days. Explore the surrounding Nishi-Shinjuku skyscraper district — a showcase of 1970s–90s Japanese corporate architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross to Higashi-Shinjuku (East Side): explore Kabukicho entertainment district by day, visit the Robot Restaurant area, and browse the eclectic shops of Shinjuku Golden Gai (tiny alley bars, fascinating even in daylight). Visit Isetan department store's basement food hall (depachika) — a feast for the eyes and palate.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Shinjuku at night — the neon-lit streets of Kabukicho, the intimate Golden Gai bar scene (try one of the tiny 6-seat bars, ~¥1,500–¥2,500 cover charge), and Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) for yakitori under the train tracks.

meals.breakfast: Shinjuku: Nakamuraya for curry bread or a bakery set near the station (~¥600–¥900)
meals.lunch: Isetan Shinjuku B1–B2 depachika: assemble a bento box from various vendors — sushi, tempura, salads (~¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho: grilled yakitori, offal skewers, and cold beer in the atmospheric smoky alley (~¥2,000–¥3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building has two towers — both offer free observation. Golden Gai bars often have a cover charge; it's worth it for the unique atmosphere. Shinjuku is one of Tokyo's busiest hubs — allow extra transit time.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (2 hours by Tobu Limited Express from Asakusa, ~¥1,400 one way). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine — an extraordinarily ornate mausoleum complex with intricate wood carvings, gold leaf, and the famous 'see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil' monkeys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Rinnoji Temple, Futarasan Shrine, and the Shinkyo Sacred Bridge. Walk through the cedar-lined avenues of Nikko's forested mountain setting. If time allows, take a bus to Kegon Falls (97m waterfall) and Lake Chuzenji.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Relax near your hotel — walk along the Sumida River waterfront near Tsukiji for a quiet evening stroll.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before departing (~¥500)
meals.lunch: Nikko: Gyoshintei restaurant for shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine in a traditional setting, ~¥3,000–¥5,000) or a simpler yuba (tofu skin) set at a local restaurant (~¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area: Tsukiji Tamasushi or a neighborhood sushi restaurant for a relaxed dinner (~¥2,500–¥4,000)

day_by_day.notes: Buy the Tobu Nikko All Area Pass for unlimited buses in Nikko (~¥2,000). Nikko entrance fees add up — budget ~¥1,300 for the main Tosho-gu complex. Start early to maximize the day.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Koenji neighborhood — Tokyo's bohemian, vintage, and indie music district. Browse secondhand clothing shops, vinyl record stores, and independent bookshops along the covered shopping arcades (shotengai). A fascinating contrast to corporate Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Nakameguro — walk along the Meguro River canal (lined with cherry trees, still scenic in late April). Browse the stylish boutiques, design shops, and cafés along the river. Visit the Nakameguro Koukashita (under-the-tracks) shopping strip.
day_by_day.evening: Continue to Daikanyama T-Site (Tsutaya Books) — an architecturally stunning bookstore and lifestyle complex open until midnight. Browse art books, design magazines, and vinyl records. Have dinner in the nearby Daikanyama neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Koenji: a local kissaten (old-school Japanese coffee shop) for morning set — coffee, toast, boiled egg (~¥700)
meals.lunch: Nakameguro: Log Road Daikanyama food options or a riverside café for pasta/salad set (~¥1,500–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Daikanyama: Ivy Place for a relaxed garden terrace dinner (~¥3,000–¥4,500) or a neighborhood izakaya (~¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Koenji is best explored on foot — the covered arcades are lively even in rain. Daikanyama T-Site is free to browse and worth visiting for its architecture alone. This is a great day to shop for unique souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets (if not visited on Day 6) in Toyosu, or explore the Toyosu Market (the wholesale fish market that replaced Tsukiji's inner market) — tours of the tuna auction area available with advance booking. Return to your Tsukiji neighborhood to revisit the outer market with fresh eyes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Roppongi. Visit the Mori Art Museum (53rd floor of Roppongi Hills Mori Tower) for contemporary art and a spectacular city view from the Tokyo City View observation deck (~¥1,800). Explore the Roppongi Hills complex.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Roppongi's vibrant Friday night scene — visit the National Art Center Tokyo (free entry to building, exhibitions vary) or browse the 21_21 Design Sight in Tokyo Midtown. Enjoy dinner in Roppongi's international dining scene.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market: fresh oysters, grilled squid, and tamagoyaki for a market breakfast (~¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Roppongi Hills: explore the restaurant floors — try Gonpachi (the 'Kill Bill' restaurant) for soba and robatayaki (~¥2,000–¥3,000)
meals.dinner: Roppongi: Tofuya Ukai for elegant tofu kaiseki cuisine (~¥6,000–¥10,000 for a special splurge) or a more casual izakaya in the area (~¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Toyosu tuna auction tours (5:30 AM) must be booked months in advance via the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Wholesale Market website. Mori Art Museum is open until 22:00 on Fridays — great for an evening visit.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura (1 hour from Tokyo Station via JR Yokosuka Line, ~¥940). Visit the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in) — the 13.35m bronze Amida Buddha, one of Japan's most iconic images. Explore Hase-dera Temple with its hillside garden and sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through bamboo groves and Zen temple grounds. Visit Zeniarai Benzaiten Shrine (wash money in the spring for good fortune). Explore Kamakura's main Komachi-dori shopping street for local crafts, sweets, and matcha products.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo. Enjoy a relaxed evening near Tsukiji — visit Hamarikyu Gardens at dusk (closes 17:00, check seasonal hours) or walk along the Sumida River. Treat yourself to a nice dinner as a mid-trip reward.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store or station bento before departing (~¥500–¥700)
meals.lunch: Kamakura: Bowls of shirasu (whitebait) rice at a local restaurant near Hase — a Kamakura specialty (~¥1,200–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji/Ginza: Kyubey sushi or a mid-range kaiseki restaurant for a special Saturday dinner (~¥5,000–¥8,000)

day_by_day.notes: Kamakura is very popular on weekends — arrive early (before 9:00) to beat the crowds at the Great Buddha. The JR Pass covers the Yokosuka Line if you have one. Bring comfortable walking shoes for the hiking trail.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Yanaka and Nezu neighborhoods — one of Tokyo's best-preserved historic districts with traditional wooden townhouses, old temples, and local shotengai. Visit Yanaka Cemetery (beautiful in spring), Nezu Shrine with its mini torii tunnel, and Yanaka Ginza market street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara for any remaining tech shopping or to pick up electronics souvenirs. Then visit the 2k540 Aki-Oka Artisan craft market under the JR tracks between Akihabara and Okachimachi — artisan workshops selling handmade leather goods, ceramics, and crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ginza for a final evening stroll and shopping. Visit Ginza Six (upscale mall with excellent basement food hall) or the Matsuya Ginza department store. Enjoy a farewell-style dinner in the Tsukiji/Ginza area.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka: Kayaba Coffee (historic 1938 coffee shop) for morning set — coffee and egg sandwich (~¥800)
meals.lunch: Yanaka Ginza: street food walk — menchi katsu (fried meat croquette), croquettes, and local snacks (~¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Ginza Six basement or nearby: Tempura Kondo for refined tempura omakase (~¥5,000–¥8,000) or a neighborhood tonkatsu restaurant (~¥2,000–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Nezu Shrine's torii tunnel is smaller than Fushimi Inari in Kyoto but far less crowded — a hidden gem. 2k540 is closed on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Yanaka is ideal for authentic local photography.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — revisit your favorite neighborhood or explore anything missed. If departing afternoon/evening: visit Nihonbashi (historic commercial district near Tsukiji) to browse Coredo Muromachi complex and the Mitsukoshi Nihonbashi main store (Japan's oldest department store, founded 1673). Pick up last-minute omiyage (souvenirs) from the basement food floors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack, check out, and store luggage at the hotel. Take a final walk through Tsukiji Outer Market for last-minute food souvenirs — dried seaweed, dashi packs, wasabi, and kitchen tools make excellent gifts. Head to the airport via Narita Express or limousine bus.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo. Reflect on 13 incredible days of food, technology, culture, and discovery.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market: one last fresh sushi or tamagoyaki breakfast (~¥1,200–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Nihonbashi Coredo Muromachi: basement food court or a quick ramen/soba set before heading to the airport (~¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Airport lounge or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport transit and check-in. Narita Express from Tokyo Station takes ~60 min (~¥3,070); Haneda is closer (~30–40 min by monorail or Keikyu Line). Declare any food items at customs when returning home. Empty your Suica card balance at airport kiosks or keep it for a future Japan trip.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo, Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. Engage with fishmongers and food artisans who have operated here for generations, offering an authentic taste of Tokyo's legendary seafood and culinary culture.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tokyo airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange private airport transfer to boutique hotel in Tsukiji, Chuo City. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your luxury accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll through the Tsukiji Outer Market to get your bearings. Sample fresh tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, and premium tuna skewers from the iconic market stalls. Pick up a matcha soft-serve ice cream and soak in the vibrant atmosphere of one of Tokyo's most beloved food districts.
day_by_day.evening: Head to nearby Ginza — a short taxi or walk from Tsukiji — for a refined first evening in Tokyo. Explore the gleaming luxury boutiques along Chuo-dori before settling in for a spectacular dinner.

meals.breakfast: Enjoyed on the flight or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Light bites at Tsukiji Outer Market: fresh uni (sea urchin) on rice, grilled oysters, and a bowl of premium tuna don from Tsukiji Sushiko or Daiwa Sushi annex stalls
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (Ginza) or Sushi Yoshitake (3 Michelin stars) — omakase sushi showcasing the finest seasonal seafood; reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag may be a factor — keep Day 1 light and enjoyable. Confirm hotel concierge has your Michelin-starred dinner reservation locked in. Carry a Suica/Pasmo card loaded with ¥5,000 for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Begin with the full Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour experience — a guided premium tasting walk through the market's best vendors. Sample fresh sushi, hand-rolled tamago, smoked salmon, pickled vegetables, and artisan dashi broth. Engage with veteran vendors who have operated their stalls for generations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Hamarikyu Gardens (5-minute walk from Tsukiji) — a stunning feudal-era landscape garden with a traditional teahouse set on a tidal pond. Enjoy a formal matcha tea ceremony with wagashi sweets. Afterward, take the scenic Sumida River water bus to Asakusa for a cultural afternoon exploring Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise shopping street.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Asakusa's atmospheric backstreets and the Hoppy Street izakaya district as the lanterns glow at dusk. Then head to a rooftop bar for panoramic views of Tokyo Skytree.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Tsukiji market fresh fish breakfast set — grilled salmon, miso soup, pickles, and rice at Nakamura-ya or Tsuruha Shoten
meals.lunch: Traditional kaiseki lunch at Hamarikyu's Nakajima no Ochaya teahouse, or premium tempura at Mikawa Zezankyo in Fukagawa
meals.dinner: Dinner at Kaminarimon Sukeroku in Asakusa — refined traditional Japanese cuisine in a historic setting with tatami seating and seasonal tasting menus

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens opens at 9:00 AM. The Sumida River water bus runs approximately every 30–40 minutes. Book the teahouse matcha experience in advance through your hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Journey to Akihabara — Tokyo's legendary Electric Town — for a deep dive into Japan's tech and pop culture scene. Visit multi-floor electronics megastores like Yodobashi Camera and Akihabara Radio Kaikan. Explore retro gaming floors, robotics demonstrations, and cutting-edge gadget shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) on Odaiba island — a world-class science museum featuring ASIMO robot demonstrations, a life-size replica of the International Space Station module, and immersive digital earth installations. Take the Yurikamome automated monorail for futuristic harbor views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Odaiba's TeamLab Borderless digital art museum (or TeamLab Planets if still operating) — an awe-inspiring immersive tech-art experience that perfectly blends Japanese aesthetics with cutting-edge technology. Book premium timed entry in advance.

meals.breakfast: Artisan coffee and fresh pastries at hotel or nearby Turret Coffee in Tsukiji — a beloved local specialty café
meals.lunch: Ramen at a premium Akihabara spot such as Fuunji or a kaiseki bento box from a department store basement (depachika) food hall in Akihabara UDX
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tableaux or Joël Robuchon-inspired French-Japanese fusion at Odaiba, or return to Ginza for dinner at Tempura Kondo (Michelin-starred) for the finest seasonal tempura

day_by_day.notes: TeamLab requires advance booking — tickets sell out weeks ahead. Miraikan is closed on Tuesdays. Akihabara is best explored on foot; wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a private guided tour of the Toyosu Market (the professional wholesale fish market that succeeded the old Tsukiji inner market). Witness the famous tuna auction from the premium observation deck — a rare and thrilling spectacle. This requires advance lottery registration, which your hotel concierge should arrange.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Shibuya for an afternoon of cultural immersion. Visit the iconic Shibuya Crossing — the world's busiest pedestrian intersection — from the premium vantage point of the Shibuya Sky observation deck atop Shibuya Scramble Square (230m high). Explore the Shibuya Stream and Shibuya Hikarie complex.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Daikanyama and Nakameguro — Tokyo's most stylish and sophisticated neighborhoods. Stroll along the Meguro River (especially beautiful during cherry blossom season in April), browse the Daikanyama T-Site bookstore complex, and enjoy the curated boutiques and galleries.

meals.breakfast: Sushi breakfast at Toyosu Market's premium sushi restaurants (Sushi Dai or Daiwa Sushi) immediately after the tuna auction — the freshest sushi you will ever taste
meals.lunch: Wagyu beef lunch at Shibuya's Yakiniku Jumbo Hanare — premium A5 Wagyu grilled tableside in an elegant setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nakameguro's acclaimed Higashi-Yama Tokyo — a sophisticated Japanese restaurant with a creative seasonal menu and an intimate, design-forward atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Toyosu tuna auction registration opens months in advance — confirm with concierge immediately upon booking your trip. Shibuya Sky tickets should also be pre-booked online. April cherry blossoms along Meguro River are spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine in Harajuku — Tokyo's most serene and majestic Shinto shrine set within a 70-hectare forested sanctuary. Participate in a morning purification ritual at the temizuya water pavilion. If timing aligns, witness a traditional Shinto wedding procession.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Harajuku's Omotesando boulevard — often called Tokyo's Champs-Élysées — lined with flagship stores by Prada, Louis Vuitton, Dior, and Japanese luxury brands. Visit the Omotesando Hills complex (designed by Tadao Ando) for architecture and premium retail. Explore the backstreets of Ura-Harajuku for independent designers and concept stores.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Roppongi for Tokyo's most cosmopolitan evening. Visit the Mori Art Museum at the top of Roppongi Hills (53rd floor) for contemporary art and sweeping city panoramas from Tokyo City View. Explore Roppongi's gallery district and vibrant dining scene.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at the hotel or a ryokan-style morning set at a local Tsukiji restaurant — grilled fish, miso soup, pickles, rice, and tamago
meals.lunch: Premium crepes and pastries at Pierre Hermé in Omotesando, followed by a light lunch at Omotesando Hills' restaurant floor or Les Deux Magots Tokyo
meals.dinner: Dinner at Roppongi's Ryugin (3 Michelin stars) — chef Seiji Yamamoto's extraordinary modern Japanese kaiseki cuisine, celebrating seasonal ingredients with avant-garde techniques

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is particularly atmospheric early morning before crowds arrive. Mori Art Museum is open until 22:00 (Tuesdays until 17:00) — ideal for an evening visit. Book Ryugin months in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko — a UNESCO World Heritage site approximately 2 hours from Tokyo by Tobu Limited Express. Explore the breathtaking Tosho-gu Shrine complex, adorned with elaborate carvings and gold leaf. Walk through the cryptomeria cedar forests to Taiyuin Mausoleum and Futarasan Shrine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko: visit Rinno-ji Temple with its magnificent Sanbutsudo hall housing three giant gilded Buddha statues. Walk the scenic path to Kegon Falls — one of Japan's most spectacular waterfalls — and take the elevator to the observation platform at the base.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Decompress with a premium onsen experience at a high-end Tokyo bathhouse such as Thermae-Yu in Shinjuku or Odaiba's Oedo Onsen Monogatari (if still operating) — a traditional hot spring facility with multiple indoor and outdoor baths.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departing for Nikko — full Japanese set with miso soup, rice, grilled fish, and pickles
meals.lunch: Yuba (tofu skin) cuisine lunch at a traditional Nikko restaurant such as Gyoshintei — a specialty of the Nikko region served in a serene garden setting
meals.dinner: Late dinner at a premium Shinjuku restaurant — Shinjuku Kappo Nakajima (Michelin-starred sardine kaiseki, surprisingly exquisite) or Tsunahachi for premium tempura

day_by_day.notes: Depart Asakusa Station on the Tobu Spacia Limited Express for the most comfortable journey to Nikko. Purchase a Nikko All Area Pass for unlimited transport within Nikko. Return train departs by 17:00 to arrive back in Tokyo by 19:00.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Yanaka — one of Tokyo's most beautifully preserved historic shitamachi (old downtown) neighborhoods. Wander through Yanaka Cemetery, a peaceful park-like space famous for its cherry trees. Browse the Yanaka Ginza shopping street for traditional crafts, local snacks, and artisan goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno — Japan's largest and most comprehensive museum, housing an extraordinary collection of Japanese art, samurai armor, ancient ceramics, and Buddhist sculpture. Arrange a premium guided tour for deeper context. Explore the surrounding Ueno Park.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shinjuku for the evening. Visit the observation deck of the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building (free entry, stunning night views). Explore the neon-lit labyrinth of Kabukicho entertainment district and the intimate Golden Gai bar alley — a warren of tiny atmospheric bars each seating only 5–8 people.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and fresh pastries at Yanaka Coffee or a morning set at a local Yanaka kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop)
meals.lunch: Ueno's Izu-ei — a legendary unagi (freshwater eel) restaurant operating since 1827, serving premium hitsumabushi and kabayaki eel in a refined traditional setting
meals.dinner: Omakase dinner at Sushi Saito (if reservations obtainable — considered one of the world's best sushi restaurants) or an alternative premium omakase at Harutaka or Sushi Sho in Shinjuku

day_by_day.notes: Golden Gai bars are tiny and intimate — some are members-only or charge a small cover fee. Respect the local atmosphere and ask before photographing. Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck closes at 22:30.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets in Toyosu (if not visited on Day 3) or explore the Panasonic Shiodome Museum and Sony Park in Ginza for a morning of cutting-edge technology and design culture. Sony Park offers interactive exhibits showcasing Sony's latest innovations and design philosophy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ginza district in depth — visit the flagship Itoya stationery store (a design and stationery lover's paradise spanning 12 floors), the Ginza Six luxury mall, and the stunning new Hermès Maison Ginza with its glass brick façade. Visit the Ginza Graphic Gallery for contemporary design exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional performance at the Kabukiza Theatre in Ginza — the world's premier kabuki venue. Single-act tickets (hitomaku-mi) are available for approximately 1–2 hours, allowing you to experience this UNESCO-listed performing art without committing to a full 4-hour program.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Café de l'Ambre in Ginza — a legendary kissaten operating since 1948, famous for aged coffee and an atmosphere frozen in postwar Tokyo
meals.lunch: Premium sushi at Kyubey Ginza — one of Tokyo's most storied sushi restaurants, frequented by heads of state and celebrities since 1936
meals.dinner: Post-kabuki dinner at Ginza Kojyu (3 Michelin stars) — an intimate 8-seat kappo restaurant serving exquisite seasonal Japanese cuisine; or Sukiyabashi Jiro Roppongi branch

day_by_day.notes: Kabukiza Theatre single-act tickets (hitomaku-mi) are sold at the theatre on the day — arrive 30–45 minutes early. English audio guides are available. Dress smart-casual. Ginza Six is open until 20:00.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Shinkansen to Kyoto for a day trip (approximately 2 hours 15 minutes on the Nozomi bullet train). Begin at Fushimi Inari Taisha — the iconic shrine with thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up a forested mountain. Hike the upper trails early morning to avoid crowds and experience the mystical atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Gion — Kyoto's famous geisha district. Walk the atmospheric Hanamikoji street and Shirakawa canal path. Visit Kennin-ji Temple (Kyoto's oldest Zen temple) and the stunning Yasaka Shrine. If fortune favors, spot a maiko (apprentice geisha) on her way to an evening appointment.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo on the Shinkansen by early evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner near the hotel in Tsukiji or Ginza.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departing for Kyoto — or a quick onigiri and green tea at Tokyo Station's premium Gransta food hall
meals.lunch: Traditional Kyoto kaiseki lunch at Mizai or Kikunoi Roan in Gion — refined multi-course cuisine using seasonal Kyoto vegetables (kyo-yasai) and pristine local ingredients
meals.dinner: Return dinner at Tsukiji area — Sushi Nakamura or Sushi Dai near the hotel for a relaxed, excellent quality omakase close to home

day_by_day.notes: Take the first available Nozomi Shinkansen from Tokyo Station (departures from 06:00). Purchase Shinkansen tickets through your hotel concierge or JR Ticket Office. IC card or JR Pass accepted. Return by Nozomi departing Kyoto around 17:00–18:00.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Digital Art Museum: teamLab Borderless in its new Azabudai Hills location — a massive, mind-bending immersive digital art experience spread across multiple interconnected rooms where art moves and responds to visitors. One of Tokyo's most extraordinary tech-culture experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Azabudai Hills — Tokyo's newest and most ambitious urban development project (opened 2023), featuring the Mori JP Tower, premium residences, a vertical garden, and curated retail. Visit the Azabudai Hills Gallery for contemporary art. Walk to the nearby Roppongi Hills complex and the 21_21 Design Sight museum (designed by Tadao Ando).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a premium evening in Azabu-Juban — one of Tokyo's most sophisticated and international residential neighborhoods. Browse the charming shopping street and settle in for a world-class dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a premium bakery — Maison Kayser in Ginza or Viron in Shibuya for French-style morning pastries and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Azabudai Hills food hall — curated premium vendors offering everything from artisan ramen to Kyoto-style obanzai (small dishes)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Azabu Yukimura or Azabu Kadowaki (both Michelin-starred) — intimate, chef-driven Japanese cuisine in the exclusive Azabu neighborhood

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless at Azabudai Hills requires advance timed-entry ticket booking. Wear comfortable shoes as the experience involves considerable walking. The 21_21 Design Sight is closed on Tuesdays and Wednesdays.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's most beloved bohemian neighborhood, famous for its indie music venues, vintage clothing stores, independent bookshops, and artisan coffee culture. Browse the weekend flea markets and discover hidden gems in the narrow backstreets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum (or Edo-Tokyo Open Air Architectural Museum in Koganei if preferred) for a deep dive into Tokyo's fascinating history — from feudal Edo-period city life through the Meiji modernization, wartime, and postwar economic miracle. Richly detailed scale models and immersive exhibits bring Tokyo's past to life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Shibuya for an unforgettable evening. Enjoy cocktails at the Trunk Hotel rooftop bar or the Andaz Tokyo Rooftop Bar in Toranomon with panoramic city views. Then experience Tokyo's world-class nightlife or a premium jazz performance at a legendary Shibuya jazz club.

meals.breakfast: Artisan breakfast in Shimokitazawa — coffee and toast at Bear Pond Espresso or a morning set at one of the neighborhood's beloved local kissaten
meals.lunch: Shimokitazawa lunch at a local curry house or ramen shop — the neighborhood is famous for its eclectic, affordable, and delicious food scene; try Spice Cafe or a local tantanmen specialist
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at Florilège in Omotesando (2 Michelin stars) — chef Hiroyasu Kawate's extraordinary French-Japanese cuisine emphasizing sustainable ingredients and innovative technique

day_by_day.notes: Shimokitazawa is best explored on foot — the streets are narrow and not suited to taxis. The weekend flea market at Shimokitazawa Station area typically runs on weekends. Florilège requires advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Nezu Museum in Aoyama — a world-class collection of Asian art and antiquities housed in a stunning building designed by Kengo Kuma, surrounded by a tranquil traditional garden. The collection includes National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Omotesando and Aoyama design district — visit the Watari-um Contemporary Art Museum, browse the flagship stores of Japanese design icons like Issey Miyake and Comme des Garçons, and explore the Spiral Building's gallery and design shop. Visit the Prada Aoyama building (designed by Herzog & de Meuron) — an architectural masterpiece.
day_by_day.evening: Final premium shopping experience in Ginza — visit Wako department store, Ginza Six, and the Matsuya and Mitsukoshi flagship stores. Head to the depachika (basement food halls) for premium Japanese food souvenirs: wagashi, premium teas, miso, sake, and artisan confections.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — take your time and enjoy the full spread on this penultimate full day
meals.lunch: Lunch at Aoyama's Anniversaire Café or a premium bento from Isetan's legendary food hall in Shinjuku — a curated feast of Japan's finest prepared foods
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Quintessence in Shinagawa (3 Michelin stars) — chef Shuzo Kishida's extraordinary French cuisine with Japanese sensibility, widely considered one of Tokyo's finest dining experiences

day_by_day.notes: Nezu Museum is closed on Mondays. Book Quintessence well in advance — it is one of Tokyo's most sought-after reservations. Use this evening to also settle any hotel bills and arrange your airport transfer for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — take one last stroll through Tsukiji Outer Market to say goodbye to your neighborhood. Pick up any last-minute food souvenirs: premium dashi packets, wasabi, artisan soy sauce, nori, or a box of exquisite wagashi sweets. Enjoy a final sushi breakfast at your favorite Tsukiji stall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, visit the Hama-rikyu Gardens one final time for a peaceful farewell to Tokyo, or browse the premium souvenir shops in Ginza's Matsuya department store. Check out of the hotel and arrange luggage forwarding to the airport if needed (takkyubin luggage delivery service available).
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer to the airport. Allow ample time for check-in, immigration, and duty-free shopping at the airport — Narita and Haneda both have excellent premium retail and dining options. Enjoy a final bowl of ramen or a premium bento at the airport before your flight.

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — fresh sashimi, tamagoyaki, miso soup, and a warm cup of dashi broth from your favorite vendors
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the hotel or a nearby Ginza café — perhaps a premium sandwich from Ginza's famous Kimuraya bakery (Japan's oldest Western-style bakery, est. 1869)
meals.dinner: Airport dinner at Narita or Haneda — both airports feature excellent premium Japanese restaurant options including ramen, sushi, tempura, and tonkatsu

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport check-in and immigration. Takkyubin luggage forwarding from the hotel to the airport can be arranged the day before (next-day delivery). Ensure all receipts are collected for tax refund processing at the airport — Japan offers consumption tax refunds on purchases over ¥5,000.
